## Objective

Get a public URL, with your secrets in the platform rather than the repo.

## Why this step exists

It's the point of the whole workshop. Everything before this was so that this
step works.

## Before you push

<Aside type="danger" title="Check this before your first commit, not after">


```bash
git status --short | grep -i env
```

You want to see `.env.example` and **not** `.env`. Once a key is in git
history it is there forever and must be rotated — removing the file later
doesn't help.

</Aside>

## Deploy to Render

1. Push your repo to GitHub.
2. Render → **New +** → **Web Service** → connect your repo.
3. Settings:

    | Field | Value |
    |---|---|
    | **Root Directory** | *(leave blank — the repo root)* |
    | **Build Command** | `pip install uv && uv sync --frozen` |
    | **Start Command** | `uv run fastapi run app/main.py --port $PORT` |
    | **Instance Type** | Free |

4. **Environment** → add `GEMINI_API_KEY`, `SUPABASE_URL`,
   `SUPABASE_SECRET_KEY`.

    This is where secrets live in production: **in the platform, not the repo.**
    Same code, different source — `app/config.py` reads `os.environ` either way.

5. Deploy.

<Aside type="tip" title="deploy/render.yaml does all of this for you">


Render → **New +** → **Blueprint** → pick your repo, and it reads the
settings from the file. `sync: false` on the secret variables means "ask me
in the dashboard, never store this in the repo".

Infrastructure in version control beats settings in someone's memory.

</Aside>

Bind to `0.0.0.0`, **not** `127.0.0.1`. Binding to localhost inside a container
means nothing outside can reach you — it shows up as a maddening "port scan
timeout" in the deploy logs.

[Full Render guide →](../../deploy/render/) ·
[FastAPI Cloud as an alternative →](../../deploy/fastapi-cloud/)

## Prove it's alive

```bash
curl https://<your-service>.onrender.com/health
```

```json
{"ok": true, "database": true, "model": "gemini-flash-latest"}
```

Two seconds, and it tells you the deploy worked *and* the database is reachable.
This is why that endpoint exists.

## Point the client at it

Open `client/index.html`, paste your Render URL into **Backend URL**, and ask a
question.

If you get **"Failed to fetch"**, that's CORS — and now it's real, because your
page and your API are genuinely different origins. Set `ALLOWED_ORIGINS` on
Render to your frontend's origin (no trailing slash) and redeploy:

```text
ALLOWED_ORIGINS=https://yourname.github.io,http://localhost:8080
```

## Connect your MCP server to Claude

Your tools are now on the internet. Add them to Claude Desktop or Claude Code:

```json title="claude_desktop_config.json"
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "research-tools": {
      "url": "https://<your-service>.onrender.com/mcp"
    }
  }
}
```

Restart Claude, and `wiki_search` and `wiki_read` appear as tools you can use in
any conversation. Same functions your agent uses — no second deployment, because
the MCP server is mounted inside the app you just shipped.

## Expected result

- `https://<your-service>.onrender.com/health` returns `ok: true`
- `https://<your-service>.onrender.com/docs` gives you interactive API docs
- The web client runs the agent against your deployed backend
- Steps stream in live, from the internet
- Your MCP tools work inside Claude

**You're done.** That URL is yours to send to anyone.

## What usually goes wrong

<details>
<summary>First request after a while takes ~a minute</summary>


Free services spin down after ~15 minutes idle. Not a bug. Hit `/health` ten
minutes before any demo to wake it.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Build fails: <code>uv: command not found</code></summary>


The build command needs `pip install uv &&` in front of `uv sync --frozen`.
Render's Python image doesn't ship uv.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Build succeeds, service won't start</summary>


Check the start command binds `0.0.0.0` and uses `$PORT`. Also check the
Root Directory is **blank** — `app.main:app` is resolved from the repo root.

</details>

<details>
<summary><code>RuntimeError: Missing environment variable</code></summary>


The variables are set in the dashboard but the service hasn't redeployed.
Environment changes need a redeploy to take effect.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Everything worked, now <code>database: false</code></summary>


Supabase paused your project after a week of inactivity. Open the dashboard
and resume — and ping it weekly if this project matters.

</details>

More in [Troubleshooting →](../../deploy/troubleshooting/)

## Where to go next

- **Keep it alive.** [The free-tier survival guide](../../deploy/troubleshooting/#keeping-a-free-stack-alive)
- **Make the background work durable.** `BackgroundTasks` loses runs on restart;
  [durable execution](../../learn/deployment-problem/#the-catch-nobody-mentions)
  checkpoints each step so a crash resumes instead of restarting.
- **Add RAG.** The `memories` table and pgvector are already there —
  [Learn · Memory and RAG](../../learn/memory/).
- **Real search.** Swap Wikipedia for Tavily or Brave in
  `app/tools/wikipedia.py`. The agent loop doesn't change.
- **Rate limiting.** Cap runs per IP before someone burns your daily quota.
